messages.author: d97d13cbd2c54501
messages.subject: batch procedures
parts:
Dear list,

I've developed a SAS procedure to bootstrap a distance survey at different
levels of effort.
The procedure generate a large file (58760 records) and Distance 5.0 spent
about 13 hours to charge the data (step 6 of the wizard) which is a bit
boring. So I tried to execute distance in batch mode (with the hope it may
run faster) using the procedure generated by Distance itself and changing
appropriately the infile statement. As a first step in my learning I
executed a much shorter file in mode "debug" so that I obtained suitable
data input and procedure files. When in Windows XP, I run a file .bat with
the following istructions:

D:\TESI\prova_import\MCDS.exe 0,dstF2.tmp
pause

where dstF2.tmp is the istructions file generated by distance appropiately
corrected for the input data file.
Every time MCDS generates 4 as output and stops. I've tried also with a
combination of " " as shown in the Distance book and also without using a
procedure but excuting directly the program MCDS.EXE. I've checked previous
answers on the list but I was unable to track the problem. Where am I wrong?

Thanks for your help,

Stefano

messages.author: d97d13cbd2c54501
messages.subject: Re: batch procedures
parts:
Dear Tiago, Len, list,

thanks for your help. Now it's working. From the last 24-hours experience I
can add 2 points which can be useful to novices like me:

1) it also works if you copy the file mcds.exe in the working directory
2) in the input file you have to list all output files potentially useful to
DISTANCE before the "options;" subcommand (names are of fantasy)

like

out.txt
log.txt
stat.txt
boot.txt
plot.txt
ris.txt
Options;

In such a way they are written in the working directory.

Cheers,

Stefano

> > Stefano, list,
> >
> > Tiago is right, it's the missing space that is critical

> > will not work
> > D:\TESI\prova_import\MCDS.exe 0, dstF2.tmp
> > will.
> >
> > I have altered the manual so it makes this clear (by adding a note to the
> > relevant page - see below).
> >
> > I'm sorry that importing takes so long in D5 - I'm hoping to have a
> > significantly faster version (but with less functionality) available as a
> > complement by the next release.
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > - Len
> >
> > Page from the manual (MCDS appendix):
> > ---------------------------
> > Running the MCDS engine
> >
> > The command to run the MCDS engine is
> > MCDS Parameter1, Parameter2
> > where
> > Parameter1 is either a 0 or a 1. 0 is for run mode - i.e. run the
> > analysis.
> > 1 is for import mode, which is used to implement part of the Project
> > Import
> > feature in Distance and is not described further here.
> > Parameter2 is the filename of the input command file - see MCDS Command
> > Language, below for details of the contents of this file.
> >
> > Example 1:
> > Assume that we have a command window open in the Distance program
> > directory
> > (usually C:\Program Files\Distance5), and that we have a file
> > TestInput.txt
> > in that directory. Then we type:
> > MCDS 0, TestInput.txt
> >
> > Example 2:
> > Assume we have a command window open in some arbitrary directory (e.g., C:
> > \). Assume that we have an input command file C:\Temp\Input File.txt that
> > we want to run. Assume that the MCDS.exe program is in the Distance
> > program
> > directory C:\Program Files\Distance5. Because both the input file and the
> > Distance program directory have spaces in them, we need to enclose the
> > program and file names in quotes:
> > "C:\Program Files\Distance5\MCDS" 0, "C:\Temp\Input File.txt"
> >
> > Note. The space between MCDS and parameter 1, and the space and comma
> > between parameter 1 and parameter 2 are critical. For example, in Example
> > 1, above,
> > MCDS 0,TestInput.txt
> > will not work (it will return the value 4 - file error) because there is
> > no
> > space between parameter 1 and parameter 2.
> >
> > Tip. An example of how to run the MCDS analysis engine from a program
> > written in another language (in this case Visual Basic) is given on the
> > Support page of the Program Distance Web Site. See also the archives of
> > the
> > Distance-sampling Email List for some messages discussing how to do this
> > (try searching for "stand alone").
